metadata.notes: Closed 2026-08-17, ROADMAP.md's own 'Explicitly deferred' SEASON entry — SALT/PEPPER/CHILI/ACID's shared shape (requiredTargetCapability: isSeasonable, addsTag, the same timing parameter) generalized into one parameter-driven verb, once the two named blocking engine features actually existed: action.ts's requiredIngredientCapabilityFromParameter and outputs.addsTagFromParameter (both added the same change, see their own doc comments for exactly what they do and why addsTagFromParameter is a value-to-tag MAP rather than a literal reuse of transformedStateFromParameter's raw-passthrough shape). ADDITIVE, not a replacement: salt.json/pepper.json/chili.json/acid.json are UNCHANGED and still used by all 18 real recipes that season something — rewriting those would be pure churn for zero functional gain, the same call this repo's DAG-execution ticket made about not migrating RecipeStep's array representation. SEASON is a genuinely new, proven-working alternative (scripts/season-as-a-robot.ts, npm run capability-test:season-verb) for a caller that wants ONE verb with a seasoningType parameter instead of four separate ones — e.g. a planner/authoring tool building a step from a variable at runtime, where 'which of four fixed verb ids do I call' is a real, awkward branch this collapses into 'which value do I pass.'
metadata.wasDeferredNote: The original ROADMAP.md entry named exactly two blockers, both now closed: (1) ActionOutputsSchema had no addsTagFromParameter counterpart to transformedStateFromParameter at all — closed, with a real, named adaptation (a value-to-tag map, not a raw passthrough — pepper.json's own notes explained why a raw passthrough doesn't work: the real tags ('salted'/'peppered'/'chili_seasoned'/'acidified') aren't the same strings as a natural parameter value ('salt'/'pepper'/'chili'/'acid'), and renaming EntitySchema.possibleTags across every entity to match would have been real, unnecessary breakage). (2) requiredIngredientCapabilities only checked presence, never identified WHICH instance satisfied it — closed via the new requiredIngredientCapabilityFromParameter field, which ALSO surfaces the matched instance id on ExecutionResult.matchedIngredientInstanceId, a real, additional capability the static list structurally cannot offer (it never varies per-call, so there's nothing case-specific to report).
metadata.capabilityMappingNote: requiredIngredientCapabilityFromParameter.capabilityByValue reuses the EXACT four capability flags salt.json/pepper.json/chili.json/acid.json already assert (isSaltySeasoning/isPepperySeasoning/isSpicySeasoning/isAcid) — not new ones. This means every existing seasoning entity (salt.json, kosher_salt.json, flaky_salt.json, black_pepper.json, chili_flakes.json, vinegar.json) is immediately usable via SEASON with zero data changes, the identical interchangeability salt-crystal-size's own closure already proved for the SALT verb specifically.
metadata.timingNote: Same parameter, same informational-only depth, as salt.json/pepper.json/chili.json/acid.json's own timingNote fields — SEASON does not collapse their four genuinely different real timing-chemistry rationales (osmosis/browning for salt, aromatic degradation for pepper, fat-solubility for chili, chlorophyll/browning-interference for acid) into one, it just doesn't repeat all four here; see each of those four files for the real citation-backed reasoning behind why timing matters differently for each.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — same reasoning as salt.json: engine.ts guards both addsTag and addsTagFromParameter against duplicates, so re-running this after an interruption is a silent no-op, not a double effect.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): same reasoning as salt.json — manual_confirmation verification matches the paper's instantaneous class exactly. requiresActiveAttention (action.ts, DAG-execution ticket) is deliberately NOT set here, matching salt.json/pepper.json/chili.json/acid.json — that field only applies to actionKind: 'continuous' (dag-scheduler.ts's own scheduleDagFromSteps already treats every instantaneous action as active by definition, per requiresActiveAttention's own doc comment, so setting it here would be redundant at best and confusing at worst).

verification.description: No reliable sensor check for 'properly seasoned' in this vocabulary — taste isn't modeled at all

hazards.note: When seasoningType is 'chili': capsaicin can irritate eyes/skin/mucous membranes on contact, even for flaked, not fresh, chili — wash hands before touching your face. Not applicable for the other three seasoningType values, but hazards is a flat per-ACTION list, not conditional per parameter value — named here rather than silently omitted, matching chili.json's own identical hazard.
